As parents and educators, I think you will find his nuggets insightful. Sons in Jesus Christ, Near or far, I am always thinking of you. My only desire is to see you happy both in this world and the next. That is why I am writing these lines from Rome on May 10th, which are intended as a sign that my heart reaches out with affectionate concern for each one. I am well aware of how much joy it gives me to be able to write letters like this and so frequently remind you of the importance we must all place upon friendship. Friendship is not just about having fun together; rather, its true value lies in being a means by which grace can come into play through our actions. The reason for my insistence on these points arises from an understanding that each one among us should always strive to be joyful and friendly towards others at all times—not only when it is easy or convenient but even more so during those occasions where we are called upon in some way, shape or form, through our presence alone if necessary. It seems clear enough then what I am asking from you: let friendship grow between us! Let this be your goal and never lose sight of the fact that every friend is a gift to God. This will help all those around them who are seeking His grace in their lives as well! Hear a certain kind of 6/8, and you think ‘horse’. It’s not really horsey, of course. There is an important distinction between the sound of real horses in music (like in The Surrey with the Fringe on Top or Horsey Horsey Don’t You Stop) and the musical topic that evokes a horse through specific musical elements like rhythm. The concept you're referring to, often called "horse gallop," is characterized by certain rhythmic patterns. Typically found in compound meter (such as \(6/8\) or \(\frac{12}{4}\)), this pattern mimics the sound of hooves hitting at a trotting pace: one strong beat followed quickly by two lighter beats. This musical topic isn't about replicating actual horse sounds but rather evoking an idea associated with horses. It's part and parcel of what makes music so rich in imagery, allowing composers to convey concepts without direct representation—much like how certain chord progressions can evoke feelings or specific scenes beyond their literal sound structure. The certificate of service of counsel states that the objection was mailed to "Barbara R. Francks, Legal Assistant Specialist" at the Washington, D.C. address as well as to the chapter 13 trustee. No response was filed by Marriott International, Inc. F.R.BANKR.P. 3007 states: An objection to the allowance of a claim shall be in writing and filed. A copy of the objection with notice of the hearing thereon shall be mailed or otherwise delivered to the claimant, the debtor or debtor in possession and the trustee at least 30 days prior to the hearing. If an objection to a claim is joined with a demand for relief of the kind specified in Rule 7001, it becomes an adversary proceeding. Read in isolation, one might conclude that mailing a copy of the objection and notice of hearing to the creditor is sufficient. However, Rule 3007 cannot be read in isolation. texts.full_text: ng Sala Daeng (, ) is the name of the intersection and neighbourhood at the beginning of Si Lom Road in Bangkok, Thailand. It is located within Pathum Wan District, next to its border with Bang Rak, where Si Lom meets Rama IV and Ratchadamri Roads. The Thai–Japan Flyover Bridge, constructed in 1992, passes over Sala Daeng intersection, as well as the westward Henri Dunant and Sam Yan intersections, along Rama IV Road. A small street, known as Sala Daeng Road, branches off Si Lom Road (near the intersection) and connects to the parallel Sathon Road. The intersection area is served by the Sala Daeng Station of the BTS skytrain'sSilom Line and the Si Lom Station on the Green Line of the MRT.
